checks.claim: The refrigerant R-134a boils at about minus 26 degrees Celsius at normal air pressure.
checks.why: Chemours' Freon 134a property sheet gives -26.06 C at one atmosphere; pressure-temperature charts agree (about -26 C).

checks.claim: A fridge compressor squeezes the refrigerant gas, which makes it hot; the condenser coils on the back release that heat into the kitchen.
checks.why: The compressor raises the refrigerant's pressure and temperature; the gas then gives off its heat in the condenser coils at the back or bottom and turns to liquid.

sources.title: Why does the outside of the cabinet feel warm (KitchenAid)

checks.claim: A capillary tube or expansion valve drops the refrigerant's pressure so it can boil and cool in the evaporator.
checks.why: The narrow capillary tube drops the pressure of the liquid by friction; the phase change (boiling) that cools happens in the evaporator.

sources.title: Capillary tubes up close and personal (ACHR News)
